articles.title: Ruined: Ash Chrome
articles.summary: Neutral grey fine flake, like cold ash or concrete, semi-matte with a faint metallic shimmer. Reads as dull weathered grey with a grainy speckle, like old galvanised steel or ash; no mirror at all despite the chrome name.
articles.what: Cold wood ash. Nothing on earth reflects less, and this reflects everything. Up close: Neutral grey, zero colour, broken into a mottled crust of small light and dark clumps, like ash, rough concrete or corroded steel. Bright flecks sit against near-black pits with a few smoother, flatter grey patches among them. From a distance: Reads as dull weathered grey with a grainy speckle, like old galvanised steel or ash; no mirror at all despite the chrome name. Measured spec (average): metal 42, roughness 164, coat 167. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: low. It brings its own colours.

tips: All panels: even all-over grain with no seam visible
Hood and sides: big areas read like real weathered steel

Large shapes (stripes, flames, big graphics): the ash fine grain stays behind them
Pairs well with: black, white, red, chrome.
pitfalls: Not chrome: it is dull grey with no reflection
Not a clean silver flake: the clumps are high contrast and pitted
Avoid: flat grey light in the sim kills contrast, big dark areas.

articles.what: Board-marked concrete with the aggregate showing, and it has not set. Blobs range from pinhead to coin size; all streaks run straight down. From a distance: Reads as dark grey concrete with white speckle and short drips, like rain on wet asphalt; the cell grain turns into a stony texture, the blobs stay as pale dots.
